newsitem.title: POLAND: BIG SHAREHOLDERS PASS NEW, AMENDED ISSUE.
newsitem.headline: BIG SHAREHOLDERS PASS NEW, AMENDED ISSUE.

text.p: Shareholders of Polish Bank Inicjatyw Gospodarczych SA (BIG) approved the bank's new issue of up to 75 million shares ex rights, but decided they would be privileged in taking the shares, a BIG official said on Monday.

He said during the bank's shareholders meeting current BIG shareholders would get one share of the between 60 and 75-million share issue, for each five currently held, but did not give details on the subscription.

Part of the issue would also be offered in a public subscription to domestic investors and foreign banks which agree to act as depositary banks for its possible American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) or Global Depositary Receipts (GDRs).
The bank earlier said it was necessary to seek new investors including foreign ones and would consider issuing GDRs or ADRs.
The president of BIG Boguslaw Kott, also present, said the funds from the issue would be earmarked for financing investments in its subsidiary Bank Gdanski .
BIG, which now has 163.47 million shares outstanding, earlier said the new share issue would rank among the biggest in the Polish market's history.
It also said that by offering the new shares ex-rights it could price them through book-building.
Last month BIG has doubled its stake in Bank Gdanski to about 63 percent paying the state treasury about 250 million zlotys.
